A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same hyperspectral reconstruction work. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction simulations, model ablations, optical-design comparisons, noise experiments, and evaluations on ARAD1K, ICVL, and CASSI measurements.

after.justification: v2 reports original reconstruction simulations, baseline comparisons, runtime and noise experiments, and cross-dataset evaluations on ICVL, Harvard, and CAVE.

M1.justification: The core patch diffusion architecture, patch normalization, scale fitting, and global optical guidance remain. However, v1 Appendix A.5 uses noise-weighted, TV-regularized guidance for noisy measurements; v2 Supplement Section 6 explicitly uses the standard reconstruction pipeline without that regularizer. This changes the noise-handling extension rather than the central method.

E1.justification: v2 removes the CASSI benchmark and high-resolution KAIST reconstruction scenario. It adds Harvard evaluation and repurposes CAVE from CASSI training data to held-out filterless reconstruction and real-versus-fake object examples. ARAD1K and ICVL remain, while the high-resolution evaluation now emphasizes cross-dataset generalization without finetuning.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds SST, SPECAT, and In2Set and removes the single-stage UNet comparator, expanding the external neural baselines from six to eight. The separate CASSI comparison, including MST-S and MST-L, disappears. The lens comparison also adds the prior rotating designs R2 and R3.

E3.justification: Default sampling changes from 50 DDIM steps with 10 guidance iterations to 20 steps with 20 iterations. Reported training changes from 72 hours on an RTX 3090 or equivalent to roughly 48 hours on an H100. ICVL finetuning is replaced by training on native-resolution ARAD1K and testing without adaptation. The noise study changes its noise-level sampling, SNR definition, and reported accuracy metric from PSNR to SAM.

E4.justification: v2 adds a systematic guidance-accuracy/runtime sweep, reports failures with 16-pixel patches, expands optical-design tests, and adds cross-dataset and real-versus-fake analyses. It removes the RGB-projection FID analysis and uncertainty-based CASSI pixel-rejection experiment, and revises the noise-robustness comparisons. Patch overlap, rescaling, and saliency analyses largely persist; the shifted-probe saliency analysis was already present in v1's appendix.

E5.justification: Both versions retain uncertainty estimation from ten reconstructions with different noise seeds. However, v1's explicit five-resample count for the noise experiment and its same-seed, deterministic sampling control for saliency are no longer specifically documented. This changes statistical reporting detail without establishing an increase in independent training runs.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises the proposed model's filterless PSNR from 34.34 to 34.63 and Bayer-plus-optic PSNR from 41.23 to 42.19. The strongest external filterless comparator changes from DGSMP at 30.04 to newly added SST at 31.77. These are revised comparisons under changed reported settings. v2 also replaces finetuned ICVL results with unfinetuned results, adds Harvard/CAVE outcomes, and removes CASSI results.

T1.justification: The main diffusion equations, scale-fitting formulation, and patch-normalization argument remain substantially equivalent. v2 adds mathematical definitions for the angular wavelength mapping and phase profile of rotating optical designs in Supplement Section 9. It also replaces v1's mean-to-noise-standard-deviation SNR definition with a power-based decibel definition.

C1.justification: The central claim of reconstructing hyperspectral images from a single optically encoded grayscale measurement remains. However, v2 drops the prominent claim of state-of-the-art performance across previous hyperspectral benchmarks and introduces a broader novelty claim about successful patch reconstruction when blur kernels are large relative to patches. The abstract and conclusion now emphasize local optical cues and reconstruction with patches as small as the PSF support.

C2.justification: Lens-design interpretation changes from approximately saturating benefits of increased mixing to an optimum followed by degradation from excessive blur. v2 adds interpretations concerning minimum patch size and wider uncertainty under domain shift. Conversely, v1's explicit limitations concerning long-range inconsistency and dependence on spatial texture disappear; runtime limitations remain and receive fuller analysis.

D1.justification: The detailed model-configuration table and core optical simulation specifications remain. v2 newly documents float16 inference and stopping gradients through scale fitting, and revises hardware/time information. It drops explicit flip-augmentation instructions and the direct project-page link, although repository availability is still asserted. Its PSF support is ambiguously described as 32 pixels in the main text and approximately 64 pixels in the supplement.

R1.justification: v2 replaces the colorization discussion with substantial positioning against patch-based diffusion research, including Hu and colleagues, Patch Diffusion, and adverse-weather restoration. It distinguishes its large-kernel setting from prior small-kernel, overlapping-patch approaches. It also expands the relationship to Jeon and colleagues' rotating optics and cites the newly evaluated reconstruction baselines.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, experimental narrative, and much of the supplement are extensively rewritten. Experiments are reorganized into separate comparison, runtime/ablation, optics, interpretability, and generalization sections. The standalone limitations section disappears, pseudocode moves to the supplement, and lens terminology is revised.

P2.justification: v2 substantially redesigns the visual presentation: it removes the separate training schematic, revises the pipeline diagram, expands the lens display, adds model-type labels to Table 1, and introduces runtime and cross-dataset figures. Saliency displays are consolidated, noise plots use different axes and panels, and extensive supplementary reconstruction galleries and CASSI displays are removed.

improvement.justification: v2 better tests the central filterless reconstruction claim through stronger baselines, cross-dataset evaluation without finetuning, and systematic accuracy/runtime analysis. These provide useful validation beyond v1's finetuned high-resolution demonstration. The net improvement is limited by the removal of explicit texture and long-range failure qualifications, reduced access information, and ambiguity about PSF support underlying the emphasized patch-size claim.
